title: 寻陆鸿渐不遇
title_en: Looking for Lu Hongjian and Not Finding Him
author: 皎然

readings.zh: “种”是栽种的意思，是动词，读 zhòng。
readings.en: Here it is a verb, to plant, read zhòng.
Zhuó huā means to bloom, so the character is read zhuó.

readings.zh: 现在读 xié。古音读 xiá，和“麻、花、家”押韵。
readings.en: Today it is read xié. In old times it was read xiá and rhymed with the other line endings.

glosses.zh: 带郭：靠近城墙。郭，外城墙。
glosses.en: dài guō: close to the city wall. Guō is the outer city wall.

glosses.zh: 桑麻：桑树和麻，泛指庄稼地。
glosses.en: sāng má: mulberry trees and hemp; farm fields in general.

glosses.zh: 篱：篱笆，用竹子、树枝编成的矮墙。
glosses.en: lí: a fence woven from bamboo or branches.
kòu mén: to knock on a door.
xī jiā: the neighbor to the west.
rì xié: the sun slants west; late afternoon.

translation.zh: 你把家搬到这里，虽然离城墙不远，
translation.en: You moved your home here, close to the city wall,

translation.zh: 却要走一条乡间小路，穿过桑麻地才到。
translation.en: yet the way in is a country path through mulberry and hemp.
By the fence you have just planted chrysanthemums.
Autumn has come, but they have not bloomed yet.

translation.zh: 我敲门，连一声狗叫都没有，
translation.en: I knock at the gate, and not even a dog barks.

translation.zh: 正要走，就去问问西边的邻居。
translation.en: About to leave, I go and ask the neighbor to the west.
The neighbor says: he has gone into the hills,

translation.zh: 每天都要到太阳偏西才回来。
translation.en: and every day he comes back only when the sun is low.

background.zh: 陆鸿渐就是陆羽，“鸿渐”是他的字（古人在名字以外取的称呼）。他写了世界上第一部讲茶的书《茶经》，被尊为“茶圣”。皎然是他的好朋友。陆羽后来在湖州一带住下，皎然去拜访他，却没见到人，就写了这首诗。一般认为写于陆羽搬到湖州以后，具体年份不详。
background.en: Lu Hongjian is Lu Yu; Hongjian was his courtesy name, a second name used by educated men. He wrote The Classic of Tea, the world's first book about tea, and is honored as the Sage of Tea. Jiaoran was his close friend. Lu Yu later settled around Huzhou. Jiaoran went to visit him but did not find him at home, and wrote this poem. It is usually dated after Lu Yu moved to Huzhou; the exact year is unknown.

author_note.zh: 皎然，唐代的诗僧，也就是会写诗的和尚，俗家姓谢，长期住在湖州的寺庙里。他懂诗也懂茶，写过讲作诗方法的书《诗式》。他和陆羽是一辈子的好朋友，常常一起喝茶写诗。
author_note.en: Jiaoran was a Tang poet-monk, a Buddhist monk who wrote poems. His family name was Xie, and he lived for many years in a temple in Huzhou. He knew both poetry and tea, and wrote a book on how to write poems. He and Lu Yu were lifelong friends who often drank tea and wrote poems together.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗写的是一次扑空的拜访，读来却一点也不扫兴。诗人先写朋友的家：离城不远，却藏在桑麻地里，篱笆边种着还没开的菊花，安静又有野趣。他敲门，连狗都不叫，可见主人常常不在家。问邻居，才知道他每天进山，傍晚才回。诗里一句没有夸陆羽，可一个爱自然、不在乎俗事的隐士已经站在我们眼前了。没见到人，反而更让人想见他。
appreciation.en: This poem is about a visit where the friend was not home, yet it does not feel disappointing at all. The poet first shows the house: near the town, but hidden among fields, with chrysanthemums by the fence not yet in bloom, quiet and a little wild. He knocks, and not even a dog barks, so the owner must often be away. He asks a neighbor and learns that his friend goes into the hills every day and comes back only at dusk. The poem never praises Lu Yu directly, yet a hermit who loves nature and does not care about worldly things stands right before us. Not meeting him only makes us want to meet him more.
